requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1.
requirements.summary: The account was absent initially, then directly observed as appworker with UID/GID 1000, home /home/appworker, and shell /bin/bash; it remained present after restart.

requirements.requirement: Set appworker login sessions to a limit of 8,192 open files.
requirements.summary: The persistent limits file specifies nofile 8192, and fresh appworker login sessions directly reported matching soft and hard limits before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Set appworker login sessions to a limit of 256 processes.
requirements.summary: The persistent limits file specifies nproc 256, and fresh appworker login sessions directly reported matching soft and hard limits before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct pre- and post-restart observations. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, the post-restart boot ID changed, and the recovered system retained the account and effective limits with no failed units. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had clear roles: creating the required account, installing its limits configuration, and performing the mandatory restart protocol. The two failed post-restart probes were read-only connection attempts. No unnecessary mutation or executor-caused residue was identified; after restart the system was running with no failed units, package health remained sound, and exposed sockets were unchanged apart from process IDs.
